title: Which Grieving Woman of the Bible Are You?
subtitle: Grief wears a different face for every woman. You're not the first to carry this, and you're not alone in it.

questions.text: How does your grief tend to show up?

options.text: As a bitterness I can taste. Even my name feels wrong now.
I collapse at Jesus' feet and let the tears fall.
A deep weeping over something my heart aches to have.
A quiet, hollow heartbreak after losing someone irreplaceable.

questions.text: When you pray in your grief, it sounds like...

options.text: Lord, life has dealt me a bitter hand.
If You had been here, this wouldn't have happened.
Please, God, remember me. Don't forget my longing.
I can't even find words. I just sit with the silence.

questions.text: What does your loss feel like at its heaviest?

options.text: Like I went out full and came back empty.
Like falling apart and needing Him to see my tears.
Like an ache for what everyone else seems to have.
Like losing the one person who was my whole world.

questions.text: How do you carry your grief day to day?

options.text: I name it honestly, even the bitter parts.
I bring it straight to Jesus and weep at His feet.
I pour it out in prayer until my lips move with no sound.
I stand watch over what I've lost and refuse to leave it.

questions.text: Which feeling sits deepest in your grief?

options.text: Bitterness, like the sweetness got drained out of life.
Raw honesty before the only One who can help.
Longing so sharp it spills over into tears.
A fierce devotion to the one I lost.

questions.text: What do you secretly hope God will do?

options.text: Restore what bitterness convinced me was gone for good.
Simply come, and meet me in my mess.
Hear me and answer the cry I've carried so long.
Bring life back where I only see death.

questions.text: When others see you grieving, they probably notice...

options.text: How changed I am, like a different woman than before.
How quickly I fall apart in front of the people I trust.
A hidden sorrow others mistake for something else.
That I won't leave my watch, no matter how long it takes.

questions.text: What would comfort you most right now?

options.text: Knowing my emptiness can still be filled again.
Seeing that Jesus weeps with me, not just for me.
A sign that God hasn't forgotten my deepest desire.
The promise that this devotion, this watching, is seen.

naomi-bitter-loss.name: Naomi (Bitter Loss)
naomi-bitter-loss.description: Your grief has a bitter edge, and you're brave enough to say so out loud. Naomi felt the same. She came home empty and even asked to be called Bitter, because that's how life felt. But her story didn't end there. God quietly worked behind the scenes and brought fullness back to her. Your honest bitterness is safe with Him, and your story isn't over either.

scripture.text: I went out full, and Jehovah hath brought me home again empty; why call ye me Naomi, seeing Jehovah hath testified against me, and the Almighty hath afflicted me?

mary-of-bethany-falling-at-his-feet.name: Mary of Bethany (Falling at His Feet)
mary-of-bethany-falling-at-his-feet.description: When grief hits, you bring it straight to Jesus and fall apart at His feet. Mary did exactly that when her brother died, saying through tears, if You had been here. And Jesus didn't scold her honesty. He wept right alongside her. Your tears move the heart of God. He doesn't ask you to hold it together. He kneels down in the sorrow with you.

hannah-weeping-for-what-she-lacked.name: Hannah (Weeping for What She Lacked)
hannah-weeping-for-what-she-lacked.description: Your grief is the ache of longing, weeping for something your heart desperately wants. Hannah knew that sorrow. She prayed so deeply that her lips moved without a sound, and others misread her grief entirely. But God did not. He heard her and remembered her. Your longing is not invisible to Him. He bends close to the cry no one else understands.

scripture.text: Count not thy handmaid for a wicked woman; for out of the abundance of my complaint and my provocation have I spoken hitherto.

the-widow-of-nain-a-son-restored.name: The Widow of Nain (A Son Restored)
the-widow-of-nain-a-son-restored.description: You've lost someone who felt like your whole world, and the emptiness is staggering. The widow of Nain knew that exact grief as she walked behind her only son's coffin. And Jesus, without being asked, saw her and his heart broke for her. He stepped in where she had no hope left. The same Lord sees you in your loss, and His compassion still moves toward grieving women.

scripture.text: And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not.

rizpah-guarding-her-dead.name: Rizpah (Guarding Her Dead)
rizpah-guarding-her-dead.description: Your grief looks like a fierce, faithful watch, refusing to walk away from the ones you've lost. Rizpah did that. She kept guard over her sons day and night, and her quiet devotion was so striking that it moved a king and was never forgotten. Your faithful sorrow is not wasted or unseen. God notices the love that keeps watch, and He honors a devotion that will not let go.

scripture.text: And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth, and spread it for her upon the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water was poured upon them from heaven; and she suffered neither the birds of the heavens to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
